title: John Rush on why directories survive AI: quality data, Reddit, and LLM SEO
summary: John Rush explains why he went all-in on directories after years of being told they were dead, why crowding shifts the win to quality, and why LLM search will send more clicks to directories than blogs. He also lays out a simple LLM SEO playbook: Reddit, top Bing and Google rankings, and social mentions.

principles.text: When a space gets crowded, the one with the best quality and work wins and the rest lose.
principles.quote: when Place gets crowded uh the the one who does the best quality and the the best work kind of wins and the rest will lose

principles.text: Spend months thinking before building; collecting ideas over time makes the build itself fast.
principles.quote: I spent like month or years thinking and then people ask like how long how long does it take to succeed and I'm like well from the moment I started building and I built it it was pretty fast

principles.text: The main reason people sign up for a product is to be entertained, so keep the process simple, one step at a time, neither too hard nor too easy.
principles.quote: I think that the number one uh Reon people sign up for a product is to be entertained

principles.text: Gamify early progress for beginners: impressions show up before clicks, so showing them keeps people moving forward.
principles.quote: Impressions come before clicks but it's cool because they already see some some progress right with impression because if you only put analytics then it's only clicked clicks and clicks come way later

principles.text: LLMs raise the quality bar; directories with really good data win, because LLMs can't invest the effort a single focused directory can.
principles.quote: directories that are winning they're having really good data right and uh that means that you have to make better directories and and and then you're ahead because LMS will be always logging behind

principles.text: To rank in LLMs, be on Reddit, on top of Bing and Google, and mentioned on social media.
principles.quote: if you want to play the game really really well you have to be a on Reddit uh B on top of the bank C on top of the Google and be on top of social media
